product: Resilia (oil of oregano DTC supplement — a full-funnel case study, not the ad itself)
hook: "12 Facebook Pages Funnel All Their Traffic to ONE Advertorial (4M+ Visits/Mo)" — scale intrigue.
body: Deep case study: single-product DTC brand running 5,900 active Meta ads across 12+ persona pages, 544 new creatives in 30 days, 4.1M monthly visits; 30–50% of ALL paid traffic goes to one 7-minute advertorial ("The CDC Says Over 60 Million Americans Are Infected With Parasites. Most Have No Idea.") telling "Lisa's" story (parasites + biofilm, why probiotics/diets/antibiotics failed, 85% carvacrol mechanism); the PDP just closes. The 6-step video script: symptom hook → hidden cause → why others failed → mechanism reveal → product as only qualifier → urgency CTA; 3–4 copy templates across hundreds of AI-avatar video creatives. OTO flow turns $30 into $83. Platform-split angles: Meta = parasites/gut, YouTube = double chin/weight loss.
cta: "Join Funnel of the Week" / comment "RESILIA" for the dashboard (membership pitch).
idea: The advertorial is the conversion engine and the persona pages are the distribution infrastructure — 12 authority personas feed one educational article that "distributes belief at scale," with AI avatars producing 500+ creatives/month.
sequencing: The scale stats (5,900 ads, 12 pages, 4.1M visits)
The advertorial reveal (30–50% of traffic → one 7-min article)
The advertorial teardown (headline, Lisa's story, mechanism)
The 12-persona infrastructure (risk split, creative flexibility, scale)
The popup + the lesson (machine, not molecule)
formatting: Very long text post; hand-graded VALUE, competitor-intel deep dive.
why_it_works: "Distributing belief at scale" — the advertorial educates the prospect into a corner where only one product qualifies, so the PDP never has to persuade; the persona pages multiply entry points (Schwartz's "same desire, different doors") while splitting ban risk.
what_to_steal: LC's advertorial architecture: one long-form "why your jewelry turns green" educational article as the belief engine; persona-style pages/angles feeding it; the 6-step script (symptom → hidden cause → why plating fails → PVD mechanism → LC as qualifier → urgency) across AI-avatar creatives.

product: commentary — no product (a Chewy UGC casting call, not an ad)
hook: "PET UGC OPPORTUNITY — 35+ (cats or dogs moms)" — casting-call header.
body: Chewy is hiring UGC creators to film a "90s advertorial video" featuring creator + pet with Chewy products; pay $2,000 + product; 224 likes, 422 replies.
idea: The "90s advertorial" is now a named retro format brands commission — the casting call itself reveals the format's demand (Chewy paying $2K+ for it).
sequencing: The format (90s advertorial video, creator + pet)
formatting: Text post + photo; casting call (422 replies = high creator interest).
why_it_works: As format evidence it's revealed preference — a major brand paying $2K per creator for "90s advertorial" videos says the retro-advertorial style is a deliberate, funded lane.
what_to_steal: LC's retro-advertorial lane: a "90s jewelry infomercial" parody format ("tired of green necks?!") — the nostalgia frame makes the mechanism memorable.

product: commentary — no product (a founder-led content listicle)
hook: "10 reasons why brands are ditching polished ads for founder faces on camera:" — listicle promise.
body: Ten reasons (founder-led before ads — Sushiswap, Gymshark; face builds trust; cheaper; algorithms favor raw; builder-thoughts build loyalty; humanizes pricing; works cross-platform; person > brand for explanations; founder = distribution channel; competitors can't copy the founder).
idea: Founder faces are the anti-polish advertorial vehicle — "competitors can copy the product, can't copy the founder" is the moat argument.
why_it_works: Reason #10 ("can't copy the founder") reframes founder content from a tactic into a moat — it's the one creative asset competitors literally cannot replicate.
what_to_steal: Jay as LC's advertorial presenter: founder-face explainer videos ("why I made waterproof jewelry") as the human front for LC's education funnel.

product: commentary — no product (a page-strategy essay; uses a fictional "Glowé Cosmetics" example)
hook: "Everyone tests creatives, hooks and angles, and almost nobody tests the page the ad runs from." — neglected-variable framing.
body: The page changes how the ad is read: brand page = advertising; a "Beauty After 40" page = content/recommendation; the playbook: build persona pages matched to angles (content page for education — "3 foundations women over 40 are switching to"; personal page for stories — "I'm 52 and this is the first foundation that doesn't settle"; review page for comparisons; community page for social proof; brand page for direct product ads); the rule: match the page to the angle; a creative that does average from the brand page can win from a content page.
idea: The SENDING PAGE is a testable creative variable — "test who they think it's coming from," not just what they see.
sequencing: The perception shift (brand page vs persona page)
The fictional example (Glowé Cosmetics → Beauty After 40)
The page menu (content, personal, review, community, brand)
The testing implication (new variable, new wins)
formatting: Long text post; essay with a worked example.
why_it_works: "People clock who's showing them the ad first" names an invisible filter every advertiser ignores — the page is the ad's source credibility, tested as a variable.
what_to_steal: LC's page matrix: run education angles from a content-style page ("Waterproof Jewelry 101"), story angles from persona pages, direct offers from @louisecarter — match page to angle.

product: commentary — no product (a 24-format lander catalog with live ad→lander pairs)
hook: "24 landing page formats printing right now (found with Gethookd API in 10 min):" — catalog promise.
body: 24 advertorial/lander formats, each with a live lander URL + its paired ad link: breaking news article, investigation piece, as-seen-on-TV, doctor warning, insider whistleblower, mainstream media roundup, founder story, transformation journal, "I tried it for 30 days," customer diary, before/after case study, mom discovery, "what my doctor didn't tell me," 5 reasons why, top-3 alternatives compared, 6 hidden causes, symptom quiz, "am I a candidate," personality-match quiz, MD-written article, Harvard study breakdown, doctor's protocol reveal, the truth about (category myth-bust) — plus a 200+ board link.
idea: Advertorials are a 24-format taxonomy, each with a live ad→lander pair — the catalog turns "advertorial" from one format into a menu of proven wrappers.
formatting: Long link-list post; 145 likes, 318 bookmarks — heavily saved.
why_it_works: Every format ships with a live ad→lander pair — the pairs make each format immediately modelable instead of theoretical.
what_to_steal: LC's advertorial menu: start with "investigation piece" ("why your jewelry turns green, investigated"), "I tried it for 30 days" (30-day waterproof wear test), and "5 reasons why" — each with LC's ad→lander pair.

hook: "There are 6 main landing page/advertorial types that print:" — taxonomy promise.
body: Six advertorial types: news mimic, story-driven, listicle, quiz/interactive, authority, comparison; full 53-format lander database linked (Notion, no gate).
cta: Doc links ("No comment or follow needed").
idea: Every printing advertorial reduces to 6 types — the taxonomy is the starting menu for LC's education funnel.
sequencing: The list (news, story, listicle, quiz, authority, comparison)
The save proof (385 bookmarks — the most-saved taxonomy in the folder)
formatting: Short text post; 175 likes, 385 bookmarks — the most-saved taxonomy in the folder.
why_it_works: Six types is a memorable, complete-feeling number — small enough to hold in memory, large enough to feel comprehensive.
what_to_steal: LC's advertorial picks from the 6: story-driven ("I wore it for 30 days"), authority ("the materials science of PVD"), comparison ("PVD vs plating, tested") — one of each to start.
